primary_proxy.denominator_note: Per-country GDELT total document count for the month. NEVER sum(topics) (Topics are non-exclusive and overlap). This makes the proxy 'fraction of THIS country's coverage that is conflict/terror', which differs from GPRC's 'fraction of ALL articles that are GPR-about-this-country' -> levels are NOT comparable, only within-country co-movement.
primary_proxy.frozen_note: Pre-registered before results and FROZEN. The verdict reads off this mapping ONLY. The alternates below are EXPLORATORY and may never claim the verdict, even if they score higher on a diagnostic metric.
primary_proxy.rationale: GPR's 8 categories collapse by subject into exactly two phenomena: war/military conflict (cats 1,2,3,4,6,7) -> t02 Armed Conflict; terrorism (cats 5,8) -> t03 Terrorism. The Threats/Acts split is orthogonal (it cuts each phenomenon into forward-looking vs realized) and introduces no third subject. So t02+t03 is the closest a-priori alignment the QGI Topic taxonomy permits to Iacoviello's war+terror construct.
primary_proxy.headline_metric: month-over-month-change (delta) Spearman rank correlation vs GPRC_<ISO3>. Levels-Pearson is trend-inflated and is a DIAGNOSTIC only.

poc_result.scope: 5 of 12 QGI countries (ARG, EGY, THA, TUN, VEN); the other 7 have no GPRC column.

affine_invariance_note: Iacoviello's published GPRC = raw_share / mean(1985-2019) * 100 is a positive affine transform of the raw share. Pearson and Spearman are invariant to a*x+b with a>0, so the proxy may be correlated against EITHER the raw-share export (this file) or the reconstructed mean-100 index with identical r. No normalization-matching is required to test shape. Levels remain incomparable for the corpus/denominator reasons above.

categories.name: War Threats
categories.definition: Words signaling the RISK of war/military conflict (e.g. 'war risk', 'military threat', 'risk of war').
categories.note: t02 Armed Conflict is the right subject bucket, but GDELT under-detects pure threat/sabre-rattling language with no kinetic event; reads as foreign-policy coverage.

categories.name: Peace Threats
categories.definition: Threats to peace / deterioration of peace, military build-ups, sabre-rattling short of war.

categories.name: Military Buildups
categories.definition: Arms build-ups, military mobilization, defense escalation, weapons/nuclear-program tensions.
categories.note: Often reported as 'defense policy', not 'armed conflict'; a known blind spot the full build should add explicit theme tokens for (GDELT MILITARY/ARMSCONTROL families).

categories.name: Nuclear Threats
categories.definition: Nuclear-weapon threats, proliferation tensions, nuclear escalation.
categories.note: Much of this is reported as diplomacy/negotiation, not armed conflict -> the most under-covered category. Material for IRN specifically (the nuclear file) -- but IRN has NO GPRC answer key, so this gap does not bias the 5-country PoC verdict; it limits coverage. The full build should add a NUCLEAR/PROLIFERATION theme set (build-plan 3.1).

categories.name: Terror Threats
categories.definition: The THREAT of terrorism / anticipated terror attacks.
categories.note: t03 Terrorism covers anticipated and realized terror together.

categories.name: Beginning of War
categories.definition: Onset/outbreak of war and armed conflict (an act).
categories.note: Realized conflict events are GDELT's strength; t02 detects these well.

categories.name: Escalation of War
categories.definition: Escalation/intensification of an ongoing war (an act).
categories.note: Realized escalation events well captured by t02.

categories.name: Terror Acts
categories.note: Realized terror events well captured by t03.

threat_act_mapping.note: Iacoviello's Threats/Acts split (GPRT/GPRA) is ORTHOGONAL to the subject mapping and does not change the topic assignment. Recorded so the full build can resolve threat vs act separately if it adds threat-language theme tokens.
threat_act_mapping.proxy_skew: The 2-topic proxy skews toward ACTS (realized conflict/terror) and away from THREATS (anticipatory risk: cats 1-4), because GDELT theme-coding tilts to events over threat language. Expect better tracking of GPRA/acts dynamics than the pure-threat component. Composition difference, not necessarily a shape break.

exclusions.status: OUT OF SCOPE - explicitly excluded from the verdict mapping
exclusions.reason: GPR is inter-state war-and-terror geopolitical risk. Domestic contentious politics (protests, riots, strikes) is a DIFFERENT risk family with NO counterpart in the GPRC answer key. Including it mechanically depresses correlation for protest-heavy/stable countries AND can spuriously INFLATE it for countries (VEN/ARG/TUN) where domestic turmoil co-occurs with external geopolitical coverage -- a confound, not signal. If the (t02+t03+t05) alternate scores higher, that reflects corpus co-occurrence, NOT evidence that protest is geopolitical risk; it must never relabel t05 as GPR.

alternates_exploratory_only.note: Adds protest; scored LOWER on levels-Pearson than primary. Exploratory only; see exclusions[t05].

Conflict-only; scored marginally HIGHER on levels-Pearson (0.6549 > primary 0.6282). DELIBERATELY NOT PROMOTED -- the primary mapping is frozen and the verdict reads off delta-Spearman, not levels-Pearson. Declining to swap to this higher diagnostic score is the anti-cherry-picking guard.

country_join.csv_country_code_format: FIPS 2-letter (NOT ISO2 -- the original task prompt's 'ISO2' label was wrong).
country_join.month_decode: xls 'month' column is an xlrd date-float (serial, datemode=0). Decode via xlrd.xldate.xldate_as_datetime(serial, datemode).strftime('%Y-%m'); special-case serial==1.0 -> '1900-01' (XLDateAmbiguous edge). Inner-join on month drops the CSV's 2026-06 (xls ends 2026-05).

data_integrity_flags.share_can_exceed_1: QGI Topics are NOT mutually exclusive; a conflict-with-terrorism article tags both t02 and t03, so (t02+t03) can exceed total_docs. 97 primary-mapping country-months had share>1.0 (max 1.83), concentrated in the 7 uncovered high-conflict countries (LBN/IRN/SDN/MMR); among the 5 verdict countries only EGY (2: 2023-10/11 Gaza onset = real signal) and TUN (7: early small-volume 2015-16). The proxy is a co-occurrence-weighted conflict-intensity share, NOT a strict probability. LOGGED, NEVER CLAMPED. Scale-invariant correlations are unaffected; it is a further reason levels are incomparable.
data_integrity_flags.guard: Assert 0<=share for every country-month; log+flag share>1 rather than silently clamp -- a clamp would hide a real topic-counting assumption.

guards_carried_to_full_build: Headline metric is delta-Spearman; levels-Pearson is a flagged trend-inflated diagnostic, never the headline.
Primary mapping frozen; alternates exploratory-only and may never claim the verdict.
No country dropping (TUN kept despite being noisiest).
No window shopping; the 2015-2019/2020+ split is a temporal-stability descriptor, NOT a gate (zero fitted parameters; per-window underpowered).
The 7 uncovered countries are NOT in any PASS/FAIL; ship them only as 'QGI-GPR (uncalibrated)', never 'GPR-validated'.

Confidence-first comms: every r pairs with the four asymmetries (different corpus / different normalization window / threat-act skew / country-attribution mechanism) and the 5-of-12 scope. Lead with 'proxy, not GPR'.
